Aphelios.watch: When Aphelios slows you with a Gravitum basic attack, immediately move out of range to avoid the root from Aphelios Q Weapon Abilites. If marked by Calibrum, back away to avoid the follow-up attack. When Aphelios can cast Aphelios R Moonlight Vigil, keep your distance from allies.
Aphelios.build: Build armor first against Aphelios’s main damage. If an extended duel makes healing from Aphelios E Weapon Queue System and Aphelios R Moonlight Vigil difficult to handle, consider Grievous Wounds next.
Aphelios.fight: Check the next weapon shown by Aphelios E Weapon Queue System, and trade during a weapon window with low burst damage. Use Draven Q Spinning Axe to empower your basic attacks, but give up catching an axe if its landing spot makes you vulnerable to Aphelios’s root.
Aphelios.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then pressure Aphelios with an empowered attack from the side while he hits minions. Before stepping forward to catch an axe, account for gank risk and check vision in the brush and river. The more passive stacks you have, the more you should look for reliable kill participation instead of an overaggressive solo fight.
Aphelios.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, then use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to move to its landing spot. Catch the axe and follow up with the empowered basic attack using Draven W Blood Rush, which has reset. After closing the distance, use Draven E Stand Aside to slow or knock Aphelios back, but save it for defense if the risk of being caught is high.
Aphelios.escape: Go in after avoiding Aphelios’s Gravitum slow and the root from Aphelios Q Weapon Abilites. While Aphelios is not holding Severum, Flash is his only way to escape, so close the distance then and land Draven E Stand Aside.
Aphelios.phase: The early laning phase is an opportunity to use Draven’s strong trades to gain kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In mid game, convert that gold into turrets and objectives. As the game goes late, Draven has fewer safe places to catch axes, so press your early advantage quickly.
Aphelios.teamfight: Keep your distance from allies so Aphelios R Moonlight Vigil does not hit multiple people. Let allies start the fight, then land empowered basic attacks with Draven Q Spinning Axe from a safe position after the enemy’s engage abilities are down. If space is tight, keep only one axe active and save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers.

Ashe.watch: Ashe W Volley is fan-shaped poke that slows, so dodge it by moving sideways and look to trade immediately after it has been used. Ashe P Frost Shot reapplies its slow with every basic attack, so do not stay within Ashe’s attack range for long. Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow can stun you, so do not start a small fight from fog of war while her ultimate is available; change direction when the arrow comes toward you.
Ashe.fight: Trade after Ashe W Volley is down and Ashe Q Ranger's Focus has expired. Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then close in from the side and land an empowered attack while Ashe hits minions. If you reach Ashe, use Draven E Stand Aside to keep your distance, but do not go for the axe if its landing spot is dangerous.
Ashe.laning: Dodge Ashe W Volley sideways, then pressure her with a basic attack empowered by Draven Q Spinning Axe. Watch for ganks when stepping forward to catch an axe, check the minimap, and maintain vision in the brush and river. Convert your early CS and Turret Plating lead into turrets and objectives.
Ashe.combo: Before a fight, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, then move to the axe’s landing marker. Just before catching it, use Draven W Blood Rush for the movement speed, then use W again after the catch resets it. After closing the distance, keep attacking while using Draven E Stand Aside to knock Ashe back.
Ashe.escape: Go in when Ashe W Volley is down and Ashe Q Ranger's Focus has expired. If Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow is also down, the stun threat is lower, and since Ashe has no ability to create distance on her own, this is an opportunity to approach with Draven W Blood Rush.
Ashe.phase: The early laning phase is a good time for Draven to gain an advantage through trades while keeping his axes active. In mid game, quickly convert that advantage into turrets and objectives. As the game goes late, Draven has fewer safe places to catch axes and becomes relatively weaker, so do not step forward recklessly.
Ashe.teamfight: Approach Ashe after allies start the fight and the enemy’s engage abilities are down. If space is tight, do not risk trying to keep two Draven Q Spinning Axe active; catch one and attack from a safe position. Save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers.

Caitlyn.watch: If you step on Caitlyn W Yordle Snap Trap, you can take heavy damage from Caitlyn P Headshot while rooted, so avoid traps in brush and narrow passages. When Caitlyn pokes with Caitlyn Q Piltover Peacemaker, stand behind allied minions to reduce the damage.
Caitlyn.build: Prioritize tenacity to reduce the root from Caitlyn W Yordle Snap Trap and movement speed to close the distance. If building resistances, get armor to counter Caitlyn P Headshot and Caitlyn Q Piltover Peacemaker.
Caitlyn.fight: While Caitlyn is hitting minions or right after she clears the wave with Caitlyn Q Piltover Peacemaker, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, move alongside her, and trade with an empowered basic attack. Give up the axe if there is a trap at its landing spot or stepping forward would be dangerous.
Caitlyn.laning: If the first fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe in advance so your first basic attack is empowered. When stepping forward to catch an axe, watch for both Caitlyn W Yordle Snap Trap and ganks, and check the minimap and vision in the river and brush. The more Draven P League of Draven stacks you have, the more you should look for reliable kill participation instead of an overaggressive solo fight.
Caitlyn.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, then move to a safe landing spot for the bouncing axe. Just before catching it, activate Draven W Blood Rush and catch the axe so you can use it again, then land your next empowered basic attack.
Caitlyn.escape: Avoid paths with Caitlyn W Yordle Snap Trap, and look for an opening to engage while Caitlyn Q Piltover Peacemaker is being cast or has just been used.
Caitlyn.phase: Both champions are strong in lane early, so trade with Draven’s empowered basic attacks without giving Caitlyn an easy kill. In mid game, convert early kills, CS, and Turret Plating into turrets and objectives. Later, Draven has fewer safe places to catch axes, so do not risk trying to keep two active.
Caitlyn.teamfight: Let allies start the fight and wait for the enemy’s engage abilities to be down, then land empowered basic attacks with Draven Q Spinning Axe from a safe position. If space is tight, keep only one axe active and save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers. If an ally is targeted by Caitlyn R Ace in the Hole and you can block it, step into the bullet’s path.

Ezreal.watch: Ezreal Q Mystic Shot can be blocked by standing behind minions, so move within the wave. If Ezreal W Essence Flux marks you, briefly move out of range to avoid the bonus damage from his next attack. When low on health, retreat along terrain to avoid the straight path of Ezreal R Trueshot Barrage.
Ezreal.build: First, get movement speed to help close the distance. Ezreal deals a mix of physical and magic damage, so if building resistances, do not focus on just one type. An option that reduces attack speed can also help reduce Ezreal’s damage.
Ezreal.fight: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then close in from the side and trade with an empowered attack while Ezreal hits minions. Make Ezreal use Ezreal E Arcane Shift, then close the distance again and fight. Give up the axe if its landing spot is dangerous.
Ezreal.laning: Move with minions between you and Ezreal to block Ezreal Q Mystic Shot while using basic attack pressure to seek CS and Turret Plating advantages. Check vision in the river and brush before stepping forward to catch Draven Q Spinning Axe. If you have many Draven P League of Draven stacks, look for reliable kill participation instead of an overaggressive solo fight.
Ezreal.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, then move to the landing marker, catch the axe, and land your next attack. Just before catching the axe, use Draven W Blood Rush so you can keep its movement speed after the catch resets it. Once Ezreal E Arcane Shift is down, use Draven E Stand Aside to catch him and keep attacking. Against a low-health Ezreal, look to finish him with Draven R Whirling Death.
Ezreal.phase: Draven is strong in the early laning phase, so build a gold lead with kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In mid game, quickly convert that advantage into turrets and objectives. Later, there are fewer safe places to catch axes, so prioritize safe positions for basic attacks over risky catches.
Ezreal.teamfight: After allies start the fight and the enemy’s engage abilities are down, move in and secure space to catch Draven Q Spinning Axe. Take control of vision and create an angle to approach instead of trading poke with Ezreal from far away. If space is tight, keep only one axe active while attacking, and save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers.
Ezreal.escape: The moment Ezreal E Arcane Shift is used is your window to engage. Use Draven W Blood Rush to close the gap, then cast Draven E Stand Aside. Keep minions between you and Ezreal while engaging, since repeated hits with Ezreal Q Mystic Shot make Ezreal E Arcane Shift come back off cooldown sooner.

Jhin.watch: Jhin’s fourth shot deals heavy damage, so back off while it’s ready. Immediately after being hit by Jhin’s basic attack or Jhin E Captive Audience, step out of a straight line to dodge the root from Jhin W Deadly Flourish. When low on health, dodge the shots from Jhin R Curtain Call, and watch for Jhin Q Dancing Grenade to bounce from a low-health minion beside you.
Jhin.build: Draven’s physical damage is effective against Jhin, who has relatively low armor, but this information alone isn’t enough to determine which item to buy first. If you need resistance, prioritize armor against Jhin’s main physical damage. Armor does not block the magic damage from Jhin E Captive Audience.
Jhin.fight: Engage while Jhin is reloading or after he has fired one or two shots. Before trading, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, then catch the axe and follow up with your next basic attack. Give up the catch if the axe will land near Jhin or in a dangerous spot.
Jhin.laning: Count Jhin’s shots and avoid trading while his fourth shot is ready. Stay away from low-health minions so Jhin Q Dancing Grenade doesn’t bounce off a kill and become stronger. Before moving forward to catch an axe, check vision in the river and brushes, and watch the minimap.
Jhin.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe just before the fight and start with an empowered basic attack. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to move to its landing spot, then follow up with your next basic attack using the cooldown reset from catching it. Once you close the gap, use Draven E Stand Aside to keep Jhin from escaping.
Jhin.escape: Jhin has no ability to create distance on his own, so reloading or having fired one or two shots is your chance to engage. When Jhin W Deadly Flourish can root you, first step out of its line to dodge it, then close the gap. If you step on a trap from Jhin E Captive Audience, move so you don’t get hit by Jhin W Deadly Flourish while on it.
Jhin.phase: In the early game, use Draven’s strong laning to seek an advantage in kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, convert that lead into towers and objectives. Draven becomes relatively weaker in the late game as there is less safe space to catch axes, so use your lead before it’s too late.
Jhin.teamfight: Let an ally start the fight, then, after the enemy’s engage ability is used, land empowered basic attacks from Draven Q Spinning Axe from a safe position. If space is tight, keep just one axe active and save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies engaging on your damage dealers. When low on health, dodge Jhin R Curtain Call, and follow your frontline when advancing on Jhin so they can take Jhin W Deadly Flourish and traps first.

Jinx.watch: Jinx Q Switcheroo!’s rockets also deal damage around minions, so don’t stand beside a minion while Jinx is farming. Dodge the slow from Jinx W Zap! and the root from Jinx E Flame Chompers!, and give up an axe landing marker if it would be dangerous to catch. If health has decreased, stay out of range of Jinx R Super Mega Death Rocket!.
Jinx.build: Jinx’s main damage is physical, so prioritize armor. Armor does not block the magic damage from Jinx E Flame Chompers!. There isn’t enough information to determine which specific item to buy first.
Jinx.fight: While Jinx pokes with the rockets from Jinx Q Switcheroo!, she has no minigun attack speed stacks, so trade with an empowered basic attack from Draven Q Spinning Axe. Close the gap when Jinx E Flame Chompers! misses or has already been used, then use Draven E Stand Aside to limit her room to escape. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to extend the movement speed bonus that resets when you catch it.
Jinx.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then land an empowered basic attack from the side while Jinx is hitting minions. Don’t catch the axe if its landing spot is dangerous, near Jinx or toward a brush. Check the minimap so you don’t lose awareness while chasing axes, and keep wards in the river and brushes.
Jinx.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, and move to the axe’s landing marker. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching it, then follow up with your next empowered basic attack as you catch the axe. If you have closed the gap after Jinx E Flame Chompers! has been used, limit her movement with Draven E Stand Aside. Look to finish Jinx with Draven R Whirling Death once her health has decreased.
Jinx.escape: Engage when the slow from Jinx W Zap! misses or Jinx E Flame Chompers! has been used. Jinx has no ability to create distance on her own, so once you close the gap, using Draven E Stand Aside makes it hard for her to escape.
Jinx.phase: Draven is strong in the early laning phase, pressuring with empowered basic attacks, so build an advantage in kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, quickly convert that gold into towers and objectives. As the game goes late, Draven becomes relatively weaker because there are fewer safe places to catch axes, so don’t recklessly push forward.
Jinx.teamfight: Let an ally start the fight, then, after the enemy’s engage ability is used, land empowered basic attacks from Draven Q Spinning Axe from a safe position. If space is tight, don’t overreach to keep two axes active; fight while catching just one. Save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies engaging on your damage dealers, and don’t start a fight just after Jinx P Get Excited! activates.

Kaisa.watch: Right after being hit by Kai’Sa W Void Seeker, its mark remains, so watch out for an engage from Kai’Sa R Killer Instinct. Back toward your allies until the mark disappears. If Kai’Sa looks ready to use Kai’Sa Q Icathian Rain, stand beside allied minions to spread out the missiles.
Kaisa.build: Prioritize armor against Kai’Sa Q Icathian Rain and her basic attacks. Kai’Sa P Second Skin and Kai’Sa W Void Seeker deal magic damage, so armor alone won’t block them. If you also struggle to deal with the shield from Kai’Sa R Killer Instinct, build magic resistance and health as well.
Kaisa.fight: While Kai’Sa is hitting minions, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, move alongside her, and trade with an empowered basic attack. If Kai’Sa engages with Kai’Sa R Killer Instinct, interrupt her engage with the Draven E Stand Aside you saved, then catch your axe from a safe position and follow up with your next basic attack.
Kaisa.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to extend the movement speed bonus that resets when you catch it. If the landing marker moves toward the enemy or a brush, don’t force the catch; check vision in the river and brushes.
Kaisa.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe in advance, land an empowered basic attack, then use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe. Follow up with your next empowered basic attack as you catch it, and interrupt Kai’Sa’s engage with Draven E Stand Aside if she uses Kai’Sa R Killer Instinct. If Kai’Sa escapes at low health, look to finish her with Draven R Whirling Death.
Kaisa.escape: Engage before Kai’Sa learns Kai’Sa R Killer Instinct or after she uses it. Pressure her then with empowered basic attacks from Draven Q Spinning Axe, and use Draven E Stand Aside to keep her from escaping.
Kaisa.phase: Kai’Sa is weak in the early game, so Draven should seek an advantage in kills, CS, and Turret Plating by pressuring the lane. In the mid game, quickly convert the gold you’ve earned into towers and objectives. In the late game, there is less safe space for Draven to catch axes, and Kai’Sa R Killer Instinct makes her engage threatening, so avoid reckless chases.
Kaisa.teamfight: After an ally starts the fight and Kai’Sa’s engage has been used, land empowered basic attacks from Draven Q Spinning Axe from a safe position. If she dives in with Kai’Sa R Killer Instinct, interrupt her engage with Draven E Stand Aside. If space to catch axes is tight, don’t overreach to keep two active; keep just one going.

KogMaw.watch: When Kog’Maw W Bio-Arcane Barrage is active, it increases his range and adds max-health-based damage to his basic attacks, so keep your distance and wait for it to end. If you’re hit by Kog’Maw Q Caustic Spittle, your armor and magic resistance are reduced, so dodge it from behind minions and don’t engage right after being hit. When low on health, move out of sight to dodge Kog’Maw R Living Artillery, and after killing him, move away from his corpse to avoid the explosion from Kog’Maw P Icathian Surprise.
KogMaw.build: Prioritize magic resistance against the magic damage from Kog’Maw Q Caustic Spittle, Kog’Maw W Bio-Arcane Barrage, and Kog’Maw E Void Ooze. Also consider armor against his basic attacks, but avoid relying on health alone because of Kog’Maw W Bio-Arcane Barrage.
KogMaw.fight: After Kog’Maw W Bio-Arcane Barrage ends, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and trade with an empowered basic attack. Kog’Maw has no ability to create distance on his own, so close the gap, then use Draven E Stand Aside to slow and displace him so you can keep attacking. Give up the catch if the axe will land in a dangerous spot.
KogMaw.laning: While Kog’Maw is hitting minions, move alongside him and pressure him with empowered basic attacks from Draven Q Spinning Axe to disrupt his farming. If Kog’Maw W Bio-Arcane Barrage activates, keep your distance and pressure him again after it ends. Before moving forward to catch an axe, check the minimap and maintain vision in the brushes and river.
KogMaw.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before the fight, then land an empowered basic attack when Kog’Maw W Bio-Arcane Barrage ends. As you move to the axe’s landing marker, use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching it, then use the W cooldown reset from catching the axe to extend the movement speed bonus. After closing the gap, use Draven E Stand Aside and continue attacking with your next empowered basic attack.
KogMaw.escape: Kog’Maw has no mobility, so when Kog’Maw W Bio-Arcane Barrage ends, that’s your chance to close the gap. Engage while dodging the slow from Kog’Maw E Void Ooze, and don’t close in during the period when your resistances are reduced after being hit by Kog’Maw Q Caustic Spittle.
KogMaw.phase: Draven is strong in the early laning phase, pressuring with empowered basic attacks, while Kog’Maw gets stronger as the game goes on. Convert the advantage you build through kills and CS in the early and mid game into towers and objectives, and play to end the game quickly. In the late game, there are fewer safe places for Draven to catch axes, so avoid reckless chases.
KogMaw.teamfight: Have an ally start the fight, then attack from a safe position after the enemy’s engage ability has been used. If space is tight, don’t insist on keeping two axes active; keep one and land basic attacks. Save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies engaging on your damage dealers. If you kill Kog’Maw, immediately move away from his corpse to avoid the explosion from Kog’Maw P Icathian Surprise.

Kalista.build: The available information isn’t enough to determine a specific first purchase. If you need to build resistance, prioritize armor against the physical damage from Kalista Q Pierce and Kalista E Rend. Be careful about choosing an item that adds a lot of health without other defenses, since Kalista W Sentinel deals magic damage based on your maximum health.
Kalista.fight: When Kalista attacks a minion, land an empowered basic attack with Draven Q Spinning Axe, then catch the axe at a safe landing point and follow up with another basic attack. When Kalista starts her basic attack animation, predict when her hop will begin and look for a chance to use Draven E Stand Aside. While Kalista R Fate's Call is on cooldown, look for an opportunity to catch her with Draven E Stand Aside.
Kalista.laning: If a fight looks likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack. Don’t activate it early when you don’t expect to fight. Don’t force yourself to catch an axe if its landing marker appears toward Kalista or toward a brush. Keep checking the minimap while chasing axes, and maintain vision in brushes and the river ahead of you.
Kalista.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and land an empowered basic attack. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe. Catch it and follow up with your next empowered basic attack, then use Draven E Stand Aside when you need to stop Kalista from engaging. If Kalista’s health has decreased, look to finish her with Draven R Whirling Death.
Kalista.escape: At that point, use Draven E Stand Aside to catch Kalista, but stop chasing if the axe would land in a dangerous spot.
Kalista.phase: Early in lane, Draven can pressure with empowered basic attacks and build an advantage in kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, turn that lead into towers and objectives. In the late game, there’s less room to catch axes safely, so watch for engage abilities when fighting.
Kalista.teamfight: Let your team engage first, then land basic attacks after engage abilities, including Kalista R Fate's Call, are used. If Kalista’s support stays beside her, spread out and be ready to interrupt them with Draven E Stand Aside the moment they engage. When space is tight, attack while catching one axe from a safe position instead of trying to maintain two.
Kalista.watch: If Kalista’s basic attacks have embedded several spears, watch for the damage from Kalista E Rend and back away from the lane until the spears disappear. Kalista R Fate’s Call can let her support engage, so create distance and prepare Draven E Stand Aside if the support moves beside Kalista. Don’t risk taking Kalista’s attacks just to catch an axe that landed in a dangerous spot.

Lucian.watch: Lucian Q Piercing Light passes through minions and reaches beyond its indicator range, so step out of the line behind minions when Lucian is farming. Lucian R The Culling can’t change its aim direction while being cast, so move to the side. Avoid trading during Lucian’s opening combo and empowered double shot, and give up axe landing markers in dangerous spots.
Lucian.build: Prioritize armor against the physical damage from Lucian Q Piercing Light and Lucian R The Culling. Basic attacks and attack speed are also central to his damage, so reducing his attack speed can help.
Lucian.fight: Let Lucian’s opening combo pass, then extend the fight after his abilities are on cooldown. Right after Lucian uses E Relentless Pursuit, pressure him with an empowered basic attack from Draven Q Spinning Axe and block his escape route with Draven E Stand Aside.
Lucian.laning: Move alongside Lucian when he attacks a minion and land an empowered basic attack with Draven Q Spinning Axe, but avoid the line where Lucian Q Piercing Light can pass through. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching an axe to take advantage of its cooldown reset on catch. Before stepping forward to catch an axe, check the minimap and vision in brushes and the river. Don’t chase dangerous landing markers.
Lucian.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before the fight and start with an empowered basic attack. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe, then move to its landing marker, catch it, and follow up with another empowered basic attack. If Lucian E Relentless Pursuit is on cooldown, catch him with Draven E Stand Aside. Look to use Draven R Whirling Death against a low-health target.
Lucian.escape: Immediately after forcing Lucian to use E Relentless Pursuit is your window to close the gap. Wait for Lucian’s opening combo to be spent and dodge his empowered double shot, then engage and use Draven E Stand Aside to block his escape.
Lucian.phase: Early on, use Draven’s strong lane trades to seek an advantage in kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, quickly turn that lead into towers and objectives. In the late game, there are fewer safe places to catch axes, so avoid forcing an engage.
Lucian.teamfight: Draven doesn’t engage first. Let your team start the fight and wait until the opponent’s engage abilities are used, then attack from a safe position. When space is tight, keep one axe instead of insisting on two. Save Draven E Stand Aside to stop an engage on your allied damage dealers.

MissFortune.watch: Miss Fortune Q Double Up hits the first target and then bounces behind it, so don’t stand in a line with minions. If Miss Fortune E Make It Rain is active, Miss Fortune R Bullet Time can overlap the slowed area, so move out of it. When Miss Fortune R Bullet Time begins, use Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt the channel or move to the side of the cone.
MissFortune.build: The available information isn’t enough to determine a specific first purchase. If you need to build resistance, prioritize armor against the physical damage from Miss Fortune P Love Tap, Miss Fortune Q Double Up, and Miss Fortune R Bullet Time. Armor can’t block the magic damage from Miss Fortune E Make It Rain.
MissFortune.fight: Move alongside Miss Fortune while she attacks minions and land an empowered basic attack with Draven Q Spinning Axe. Immediately after she last-hits a minion, create distance to avoid her next poke. Close the gap when Miss Fortune E Make It Rain is on cooldown or when you can fight outside its area. Once you’re close, use Draven E Stand Aside to slow and displace her, preventing her escape.
MissFortune.laning: If a fight looks likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, and stand beside minions to avoid Miss Fortune Q Double Up. Don’t force yourself to catch an axe if its landing marker bounces toward Miss Fortune or into a brush. Check the minimap before stepping forward to catch an axe, and maintain vision in brushes and the river.
MissFortune.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, then move to a safe axe landing marker. Activate Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe, then use W again after the catch resets its cooldown and land your next empowered basic attack. If Miss Fortune runs away or casts Miss Fortune R Bullet Time, use Draven E Stand Aside to catch her or interrupt the channel.
MissFortune.escape: Miss Fortune has no mobility ability, so look for a chance to close the gap after dodging the slow from Miss Fortune E Make It Rain. If she uses Miss Fortune W Strut to escape, hit her once to reset the movement speed boost, then use Draven E Stand Aside when you’re close.
MissFortune.phase: Early on, use Draven’s strong lane trades to seek an advantage in kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, turn the gold you’ve earned into towers and objectives. Draven becomes relatively weaker as the game goes on because there are fewer safe places to catch axes, so consolidate your early advantage quickly.
MissFortune.teamfight: Don’t start a fight in the area covered by Miss Fortune E Make It Rain; wait for an opportunity outside it. Let your team start the fight and attack with Draven Q Spinning Axe from a safe position after the opponent’s engage abilities are used. When Miss Fortune R Bullet Time begins, interrupt it with Draven E Stand Aside. If you can’t interrupt it, move to the side of the cone.

Samira.build: Consider armor items first. Samira’s main damage is physical, so armor is effective, but it can’t block the magic damage from Samira P Daredevil Impulse and Samira E Wild Rush.
Samira.fight: When Samira attacks a minion, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and pressure her first with a basic attack. Hold your attacks while Samira W Blade Whirl is active. Once the spin ends, catch your axe and attack again. If Samira engages with E Wild Rush, use the Draven E Stand Aside you saved to interrupt her dash.
Samira.laning: Poke with basic attacks while denying Samira the chance to walk into range and attack you in melee. Give up the catch if an axe lands in a dangerous spot toward Samira. Before stepping forward to catch an axe, check the minimap and your vision in the river and brushes.
Samira.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before the fight, land an empowered basic attack, then move to the landing marker, catch the axe, and follow up with another basic attack. Activate Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to use its cooldown reset on catch. Stop basic attacks while Samira W Blade Whirl is active, and use Draven E Stand Aside against Samira E Wild Rush or Samira R Inferno Trigger.
Samira.escape: If Samira used Samira E Wild Rush and no one died, that’s your chance to close the gap and attack before her dash resets. If an opponent beside Samira uses crowd control, dodge it before engaging, then use Draven E Stand Aside to stop Samira’s movement.
Samira.phase: Early in lane is a good time for Draven to build an advantage with empowered basic attacks from Draven Q Spinning Axe. In the mid game, turn that lead into towers and objectives. In the late game, there are fewer safe places to catch axes, so don’t force yourself forward.
Samira.teamfight: Let your team start the fight, then attack from a safe position after Samira’s engage abilities are used. When space is tight, keep one axe instead of insisting on two. If Samira R Inferno Trigger begins or she dashes onto an allied damage dealer, interrupt her with Draven E Stand Aside. When retreating, don’t leave a low-health ally behind.
Samira.watch: Samira W Blade Whirl blocks basic attacks and projectiles while active, so attack after it ends. Watch for Samira’s follow-up attacks if she closes in with Samira E Wild Rush or an ally is crowd controlled. When Samira R Inferno Trigger starts, knock her back with Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt the shots.

Senna.watch: Senna Q Piercing Darkness travels in a straight line through allies or minions, so move out of the line between Senna and her target. Dodge Senna W Last Embrace from behind minions, and if it hits you, move away from allies before the root detonates. After being hit once, dodge the follow-up attack to deny Senna P Absolution mist.
Senna.build: Build armor first because Senna’s main damage is physical. Senna P Absolution deals damage based on the target’s current health, so build armor along with health instead of stacking health alone.
Senna.fight: When Senna steps forward to collect a soul, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and start trading with empowered basic attacks. If you’ve dodged Senna W Last Embrace and closed the gap, use Draven E Stand Aside to catch her with its slow and displacement, then continue with basic attacks. If the axe would land in a dangerous spot, give up the catch.
Senna.laning: Early on, keep your axes spinning and pressure the spots where Senna steps up to farm minions or collect souls. Position behind minions so you can dodge the straight paths of Senna Q Piercing Darkness and Senna W Last Embrace. Before stepping forward to catch an axe, check the minimap and secure vision in the river and nearby bushes.
Senna.combo: Just before a fight, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered attack, then move toward its landing marker. Cast Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to gain movement speed, so you can use W again after the catch resets it. Once you’re on Senna, pin her down with Draven E Stand Aside and land your next empowered attack.
Senna.escape: A missed Senna W Last Embrace is your chance to close the gap. Senna has no ability to create distance on her own, so approach with Draven W Blood Rush and catch her with Draven E Stand Aside. If you see Senna E Curse of the Black Mist, enemies inside it may approach together, so first retreat to an area where you have vision.
Senna.phase: Early on, use Draven’s strong laning to deny Senna souls. In mid game, convert the gains from kills, CS, and Turret Plating earned during laning into towers and objectives. In late game, Senna’s range and attack damage grow while safe spots for Draven to catch axes become scarcer, so press your early advantage quickly.
Senna.teamfight: Don't engage first. Wait for an ally to initiate and the enemy's engage ability to be used, then attack from a safe position with empowered basic attacks. If space is tight, keep only one axe active and save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies who dive onto your allied damage dealers. If Senna E Curse of the Black Mist appears, back away to secure vision or use Draven R Whirling Death to deter an engage from within the mist.

Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots slowed targets and stuns immobilized targets. If you are slowed, give up the axe landing spot and move out of the straight line in front of Seraphine. Seraphine R Encore gains range each time it hits an allied champion, so don’t stand in a line with your allies.
Seraphine.build: Prioritize magic resistance against the magic damage from Seraphine P Stage Presence, Q High Note, and E Beat Drop. If you’re likely to be repeatedly caught by Seraphine’s immobilizing effects, take Cleanse instead of Barrier. If Cleanse isn’t enough, consider Mercurial Scimitar between core items.
Seraphine.fight: Trade right after dodging Seraphine E Beat Drop or when Seraphine is alone and separated from her allies. Pressure her with empowered attacks from Draven Q Spinning Axe, but give up the catch if the axe lands in a dangerous spot near her. After closing the gap, use Draven E Stand Aside to stop Seraphine from escaping.
Seraphine.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack. Pressure Seraphine with empowered basic attacks when she is separated from her ranged damage dealer, and don’t force a catch on an axe that lands forward while Seraphine E Beat Drop is still available. Before stepping out to catch an axe, check the minimap and maintain vision in the bushes and river.
Seraphine.combo: After dodging Seraphine E Beat Drop, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and land an empowered attack. Activate Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the bouncing axe, then follow up with your next empowered attack. If you’ve closed the gap, use Draven E Stand Aside to stop Seraphine from escaping.
Seraphine.escape: Seraphine has no mobility ability, so the moment after Seraphine E Beat Drop is used is your chance to close the gap. If you’re slowed, first move out of the straight line in front of Seraphine, and give up any dangerous axe landing spots.
Seraphine.phase: Draven is strong in the early lane, so build a lead with kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In mid game, quickly convert the gold you’ve earned into towers and objectives. In late game, safe spots to catch axes become scarcer and Draven gets relatively weaker, so don’t overextend forward.
Seraphine.teamfight: Join after an ally starts the fight and Seraphine’s catching ability has been used. Seraphine R Encore can extend its reach through your allies, so spread out to either side of them. If space is tight, don’t insist on keeping two axes spinning; keep one and attack from a safe position.

Sivir.watch: Watch the path of Sivir Q Boomerang Blade and dodge so it doesn’t hit you on either the way out or the return. If Sivir E Spell Shield is available, it can block Draven E Stand Aside, so bait it out first. Avoid long chases while Sivir R On The Hunt is active.
Sivir.build: Build armor first against the damage from Sivir Q Boomerang Blade and Sivir W Ricochet. Since Sivir’s damage relies on basic attacks and attack speed, also consider ways to reduce her attack speed.
Sivir.fight: When Sivir attacks minions, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, move alongside her, and trade with empowered attacks. Once Sivir E Spell Shield is down and you’ve closed the gap, catch her with Draven E Stand Aside. Give up the axe if its landing spot is dangerous.
Sivir.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe. Account for Sivir’s fast wave clear: before leaving lane, push it first or make sure an ally is ready to catch it. Check the minimap and river vision before stepping forward to catch an axe.
Sivir.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and land an empowered attack, then use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe and move toward its landing marker. Catch the axe and land your next empowered attack, then use Draven E Stand Aside after Sivir E Spell Shield is down. If Sivir retreats at low health, look to finish her with Draven R Whirling Death.
Sivir.escape: When Sivir E Spell Shield is down, you have an opening to engage with Draven E Stand Aside. Sivir has no teleporting mobility ability or skill that creates distance on her own, so close the gap and catch her. Avoid a long chase if Sivir R On The Hunt is active.
Sivir.phase: Early on, use Draven’s strong trades to aim for a lead in kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In mid game, quickly convert that lead into towers and objectives. In late game, safe spots to catch axes become scarcer, so avoid forcing your way in.
Sivir.teamfight: Let an ally engage first, then find a position to attack after the enemy’s engage ability is used. If space is tight, keep only one Draven Q Spinning Axe active and attack from a safe spot; save Draven E Stand Aside to peel enemies off your allied damage dealers. Look for an opening to catch Sivir when Sivir E Spell Shield is down.

Smolder.watch: Smolder W Achooo! explodes when it hits a champion, granting him a stacking growth buff and slowing you. Dodge by standing behind minions or moving to the side. When Smolder R MMOOOMMMM! lands, move out of the center and the flames at Smolder’s feet, then re-engage. Smolder Q Super Scorcher Breath gains true damage and an execute as it stacks, so be especially careful at low health.
Smolder.build: Build armor first because Smolder R MMOOOMMMM!’s main damage is physical. Armor cannot block the magic damage from Smolder P Dragon Practice or the true damage from Smolder Q Super Scorcher Breath. Smolder Q Super Scorcher Breath also deals damage based on your maximum health, so be careful about relying on a large health pool alone.
Smolder.fight: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then move alongside Smolder while he attacks minions and trade with empowered attacks. Bait out Smolder E Flap, Flap, Flap, then close the gap and look for a chance to interrupt his movement with Draven E Stand Aside. Give up the catch if the axe lands in a dangerous spot.
Smolder.laning: Smolder has low health and armor early, and grows stronger as he stacks Smolder P Dragon Practice, so pressure him from the start to deny him easy CS. Empower your attacks with Draven Q Spinning Axe and trade, but watch for ganks when stepping forward to catch an axe. Check the minimap often and maintain vision in the bushes and river on the side where you’re pushing.
Smolder.combo: Before a fight, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered attack, then move toward the axe’s landing spot. Cast Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to gain movement speed, and use the reset to activate W again for the next axe. Once Smolder E Flap, Flap, Flap is down, pressure him and interrupt his movement with Draven E Stand Aside. Look to finish an enemy escaping at low health with Draven R Whirling Death.
Smolder.escape: Smolder E Flap, Flap, Flap is his only escape, so the moment after he uses it is your chance to engage. Approach after dodging Smolder W Achooo! so you can trade without taking its slow or giving him a growth stack. Save Draven E Stand Aside for the moment you can interrupt Smolder E Flap, Flap, Flap.
Smolder.phase: Early on, Draven’s empowered attacks are strong and Smolder has few growth stacks, so build a lane lead. In mid game, convert that lead into towers and objectives to close out the game quickly. In late game, Smolder’s permanent growth stacks accumulate and Draven has less room to catch axes safely, putting you at a disadvantage.
Smolder.teamfight: Draven should not engage first. Wait for an ally to start the fight and for the enemy’s engage ability to be used, then attack from a safe position. If there’s little room to catch axes, don’t insist on keeping two Draven Q Spinning Axes active; keep one. Save Draven E Stand Aside to peel enemies off your allied damage dealers, and when Smolder R MMOOOMMMM! lands, move out of the flames before attacking again.

Tristana.watch: Tristana W Rocket Jump is used to engage and disengage, so be ready to interrupt her with Draven E Stand Aside as she jumps. Tristana R Buster Shot stuns and knocks back, so don’t force an engage while both it and W Rocket Jump are available. Keep your distance from allied minions to avoid the area damage from Tristana E Explosive Charge.
Tristana.fight: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and trade empowered attacks from the side while Tristana hits minions. Bait out Tristana W Rocket Jump, then close the distance; if she jumps back in, interrupt her midair with Draven E Stand Aside. Don’t chase if the axe landing spot is dangerous.
Tristana.laning: Early on, push the wave toward Tristana’s turret to make last-hitting harder. Don’t stand right next to allied minions, and check vision in the river and bushes before stepping forward to catch an axe. Convert your lead into pressure on turrets and objectives.
Tristana.combo: Before a fight, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered attack, then move to the landing spot to catch the axe and attack again. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to take advantage of the cooldown reset on pickup. Save Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt Tristana W Rocket Jump, and look to finish low-health enemies with Draven R Whirling Death.
Tristana.escape: The moment after Tristana uses W Rocket Jump is your chance to close the distance. Don’t engage carelessly while Tristana W Rocket Jump and R Buster Shot are both available; engage when you can interrupt her jump with Draven E Stand Aside.
Tristana.phase: In the early laning phase, pressure Tristana by using Draven’s strong trades and her weak early game. In the mid game, turn the gold you earned early into turrets and objectives to accelerate the game. In the late game, safe spots to catch axes become scarce, and it becomes hard for Draven to deal with a fully built Tristana.
Tristana.teamfight: Attack after your team starts a fight and Tristana’s engage ability is on cooldown. If space is tight, keep only one axe and attack from a safe spot; use Draven E Stand Aside to stop her engage. If an ally dies and Tristana W Rocket Jump resets, retreat immediately.

Twitch.build: Get a Control Ward early to prepare for Twitch Q Ambush. Twitch E Contaminate deals both types of damage, so building only one type of resistance blocks only part of it; resistance can’t reduce the true damage from Twitch P Deadly Venom. After that, consider ways to increase your total health and reduce Twitch’s attack speed.
Twitch.fight: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then trade empowered attacks from the side while Twitch hits minions. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching an axe so the movement speed boost refreshed on pickup continues. If Twitch W Venom Cask lands at your feet, leave the cloud even if you have to abandon the axe.
Twitch.laning: Don’t force a catch if the axe landing spot is toward Twitch or in a bush without vision. Check the minimap and maintain vision in the bushes and river when stepping forward to catch an axe. Alert your allies if Twitch disappears from lane, as he may rotate to another lane.
Twitch.combo: Before a fight, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered attack, then move to the axe’s landing spot. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching it, then follow up with another empowered attack. When Twitch Q Ambush ends and the distance has been closed, use Draven E Stand Aside to slow and displace him; if he retreats at low health, look to finish him with Draven R Whirling Death.
Twitch.escape: Twitch has no ability to create distance on his own, so close in when Twitch Q Ambush ends and reveals his position. Approach with Draven W Blood Rush from a spot outside Twitch W Venom Cask’s slow, then use Draven E Stand Aside once you’re close.
Twitch.phase: Early on, use Draven’s strong laning to seek an advantage in CS and Turret Plating, and turn kills into gold from Draven P League of Draven stacks. In the mid game, quickly convert that lead into turrets and objectives. In the late game, safe spots to catch axes become scarce, so avoid forced engages and watch for the range and piercing attacks from Twitch R Spray and Pray.
Twitch.teamfight: Let an ally start the fight and wait for the enemy’s engage to be used, then attack from a safe position while keeping Draven Q Spinning Axe active. Focus the same target as your allies when Twitch Q Ambush ends or Twitch activates R Spray and Pray and takes position. Spread sideways from the direction of Twitch R Spray and Pray’s attacks, and save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies who dive onto your allied damage dealers.
Twitch.watch: If Twitch Q Ambush makes him disappear from vision, use a Control Ward to secure vision, and don’t enter bushes you can’t see into. If Twitch W Venom Cask hits you, leave it immediately. After taking several basic attacks, create distance to guard against Twitch E Contaminate even if you still have health. Account for Twitch R Spray and Pray’s increased range, and don’t stand in a line with your allies.

TwistedFate.watch: If Twisted Fate is holding a yellow card with W Pick a Card, his next basic attack will stun you, so stay outside his basic attack range. Take less damage from Twisted Fate Q Wild Cards by standing behind minions.
TwistedFate.build: The information provided isn’t enough to identify a specific first item. Twisted Fate Q Wild Cards, W Pick a Card, and E Stacked Deck all deal magic damage, so choose magic resistance if you’re building resistance. If the enemy team has multiple crowd-control abilities that can lock Draven down, take Cleanse instead of Barrier; if that isn’t enough, fit Mercurial Scimitar between your core items.
TwistedFate.fight: When Twisted Fate W Pick a Card’s yellow card has been used, or he’s holding a blue or red card, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and trade with empowered attacks. Don’t catch the axe if its landing spot is dangerous. If Twisted Fate R Destiny appears within range, interrupt his movement with Draven E Stand Aside.
TwistedFate.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then move alongside the enemy while they hit minions and land an empowered attack. Watch for ganks when stepping forward to catch an axe, and check the minimap and vision in the river and bushes.
TwistedFate.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered attack, then move to a safe landing marker to catch the axe and attack again. If you use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe, the pickup resets its cooldown so you can keep the movement speed boost going. If Twisted Fate is low on health and you have many Draven P League of Draven stacks, look to execute him with Draven R Whirling Death.
TwistedFate.phase: Early on, use Draven’s strong laning to build an advantage in CS and Turret Plating. In the late game, Draven becomes relatively weaker as safe spots to catch axes become scarce, so avoid risky solo fights.
TwistedFate.teamfight: Have your team start the fight and wait for the enemy’s engage ability to be used before Draven moves in to attack. If space is tight, don’t insist on keeping two axes; safely maintain just one. Use Draven E Stand Aside to stop an enemy diving onto an allied damage dealer, or to interrupt a visible Twisted Fate R Destiny within range.
TwistedFate.escape: If Twisted Fate has also just used the gold card from W Pick a Card, close in, cast Draven E Stand Aside, and follow up with empowered basic attacks.

Varus.watch: If you’re hit by Varus’s abilities while Blighted Quiver stacks are on you, you take bonus damage based on your maximum health. After taking a few basic attacks, retreat to give the Blight time to wear off, then reengage. If an ally is caught by Varus R Chain of Corruption, don’t approach; stay far enough away that the tendrils can’t reach you.
Varus.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Varus Q Piercing Arrow and Varus E Hail of Arrows. Armor won’t block Varus W Blighted Quiver or Varus R Chain of Corruption, and Varus W Blighted Quiver deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid relying on a large health increase alone.
Varus.fight: When Varus aims Varus Q Piercing Arrow, sidestep its path while closing the distance. Once you’re close, trade with empowered attacks from Draven Q Spinning Axe; if you’ve taken several of Varus’s basic attacks, retreat until the Blight wears off. Varus has no ability to create distance on his own, so after closing in, use Draven E Stand Aside to slow and displace him.
Varus.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then land an empowered attack from the side while Varus hits minions. Abandon the axe if its landing spot is dangerously positioned toward Varus or a bush. Check the minimap and maintain wards in the bushes and river in that direction when stepping forward to catch an axe.
Varus.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and attack, then move to the axe’s landing marker. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching it, then follow up with an empowered attack after the pickup resets its cooldown. Use Draven E Stand Aside when you close the distance to Varus, and look to execute a low-health Varus with Draven R Whirling Death.
Varus.escape: The chance to close the distance comes when Varus R Chain of Corruption is on cooldown or while Varus is aiming Varus Q Piercing Arrow. While he aims, dodge sideways from the arrow’s path as you approach; then use the fact that Varus has no ability to create distance on his own and land Draven E Stand Aside.
Varus.phase: The early laning phase is Draven’s strength, so build a lead through kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, turn that gold into turrets and objectives. In the late game, safe spots to catch axes become scarce and Draven becomes relatively weaker, so don’t chase dangerous landing spots.
Varus.teamfight: Have your team start the fight and wait for the enemy’s engage ability to be used before moving in to land empowered attacks with Draven Q Spinning Axe from a safe spot. If space is tight, don’t insist on maintaining two axes; keep just one going, and save Draven E Stand Aside to stop enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers. Spread out so Varus R Chain of Corruption doesn’t spread to nearby allies, and wait out the few seconds when Varus becomes stronger after getting a kill or assist before fighting again.

Vayne.watch: Avoid fighting with your back to a wall so Vayne E Condemn cannot pin you against it and stun you. Vayne W Silver Bolts deals true damage based on the target’s max health after repeated attacks on the same target, so step out of range just before it triggers. During Vayne R Final Hour, Vayne Q Tumble briefly makes her invisible each time, so reacquire her position before attacking.
Vayne.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Vayne Q Tumble and Vayne E Condemn. Vayne W Silver Bolts’ true damage is not reduced by armor and scales with max health, so avoid relying on large health boosts alone. Also consider items that reduce her attack speed so you take fewer basic attacks.
Vayne.fight: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe ahead of time and trade with empowered basic attacks from the side while Vayne attacks minions. Close the distance right after Vayne Q Tumble is used, then use Draven E Stand Aside to disrupt her movement. Give up the axe if its landing point is near a wall or otherwise dangerous.
Vayne.laning: In the early game, pressure the lane and disrupt Vayne’s farming by exploiting her low health and armor. Draven’s physical damage also deals well with her low armor. When stepping forward to catch an axe, watch for ganks, check the minimap, and maintain vision in the brush and river.
Vayne.combo: Before a trade, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, then move to the landing marker. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe, then keep moving with the refreshed movement speed. Once Vayne Q Tumble is used, use Draven E Stand Aside to disrupt her movement and follow up with empowered basic attacks.
Vayne.phase: Draven is strong in the early laning phase, so build an advantage with kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, convert that advantage into turrets and objectives. In the late game, the matchup worsens as Vayne completes her items and Draven has less room to catch axes safely.
Vayne.teamfight: Have your team start the fight, then attack from a safe position after Vayne has used her engage ability. Avoid narrow passages and areas near walls; if space is limited, keep only one axe active. Save Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers.
Vayne.escape: The moment Vayne Q Tumble is used is your chance to close the gap. Engage from a position where Vayne E Condemn can’t stun you against a wall, then use Draven E Stand Aside. Don’t chase into a dangerous position just to catch an axe.

Xayah.watch: Xayah E Bladecaller roots you if you’re hit by at least three returning feathers. Move sideways immediately if three or more feathers form a line connecting you and Xayah. Don’t use Draven E Stand Aside too early while Xayah R Featherstorm is available.
Xayah.build: The source provides no specific item recommendations. When building resistances, prioritize armor because Xayah’s primary damage is physical.
Xayah.fight: While Xayah attacks minions, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and trade briefly with empowered basic attacks. Keep moving sideways instead of staying in one place to avoid the path of feathers returning from Xayah E Bladecaller.
Xayah.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack. Give up the axe if its landing point is toward Xayah or in a dangerous spot. When stepping forward to catch an axe, check the minimap and maintain vision in the brush and river.
Xayah.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and land a basic attack, then use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe. Move sideways as you catch it to leave the path of Xayah’s returning feathers, then land your next empowered basic attack. After Xayah R Featherstorm is used, use Draven E Stand Aside to help engage.
Xayah.escape: If at least three feathers are on the ground along the return path, dodge Xayah E Bladecaller before engaging.
Xayah.phase: Draven’s lane pressure is strongest in the early game, so look for an advantage in kills and CS. In the mid game, convert your gold lead into turrets and objectives. As the game goes late, there are fewer safe places to catch axes, so avoid forcing engages.
Xayah.teamfight: Have your team start the fight, then attack from a safe position after Xayah R Featherstorm is used. If space is tight, don’t risk trying to keep two axes active; use just one. Save Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers.

Zeri.watch: Zeri W Ultrashock Laser spreads widely when it hits terrain, so don’t stand with your back to a wall or face her head-on in a narrow passage. Zeri E Spark Surge travels farther when crossing a wall, so don’t push her toward one. After Zeri R Lightning Crash activates, don’t chase her, and watch your health so you don’t enter the execute range of Zeri P Living Battery.
Zeri.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Zeri Q Burst Fire and Zeri W Ultrashock Laser. Zeri P Living Battery and Zeri E Spark Surge deal magic damage that armor cannot block, so keep health in mind as well. Draven’s physical damage is effective against Zeri’s low armor.
Zeri.fight: While Zeri attacks minions, trade with basic attacks empowered by Draven Q Spinning Axe, catching the axe from a safe position. Close the distance right after she uses Zeri E Spark Surge; if she is dashing, interrupt her with the Draven E Stand Aside you saved.
Zeri.laning: Use Zeri’s short basic attack range to build a CS and Turret Plating lead before she completes her core items. If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack. Don’t force a catch if the landing marker points toward Zeri or into a brush. When stepping forward to catch an axe, check the minimap and maintain vision in the brush and river.
Zeri.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe ahead of time, land an empowered basic attack, then move to the landing marker. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe, then use the cooldown reset from catching it to follow up with another empowered basic attack. Save Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt Zeri E Spark Surge.
Zeri.escape: The moment after Zeri E Spark Surge is used is your chance to close the distance. Approach in open terrain, and hit Zeri with Draven E Stand Aside while she is dashing to interrupt her movement. If Zeri R Lightning Crash is active, don’t try to catch her on foot.
Zeri.phase: Draven is strong in the early laning phase, so get ahead with kills, CS, and Turret Plating before Zeri completes her core items. In the mid game, convert your gold lead into turrets and objectives. In the late game, there are fewer safe places for Draven to catch axes, and it becomes harder to pick off Zeri, so avoid chasing too far.
Zeri.teamfight: Have your team start the fight, then land empowered basic attacks with Draven Q Spinning Axe from a safe position after the enemy has used their engage ability. If space is tight, don’t risk trying to keep two axes active; use just one. Save Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers, and don’t chase Zeri while Zeri R Lightning Crash is active.

Ziggs.fight: Close the distance after Ziggs uses a full set of abilities, especially right after he uses Ziggs's W Satchel Charge to poke or clear the wave. Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and land an empowered basic attack, but give up the axe if its landing point is inside Ziggs's E Hexplosive Minefield.
Ziggs.laning: If a fight is likely, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe before your first basic attack, then pressure Ziggs from the side while he attacks minions. Before stepping forward to catch an axe, check the minimap and vision in the river and brush. Convert early CS and Turret Plating advantages into turrets and objectives.
Ziggs.combo: Activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and land an empowered basic attack, then move to a safe landing marker. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe, then use the W cooldown reset from catching it to follow up with another empowered basic attack. If Ziggs tries to escape with Ziggs's W Satchel Charge, use Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt his movement.
Ziggs.teamfight: Have your team start the fight, then land basic attacks from a safe position after Ziggs has used a mobility ability such as Ziggs's W Satchel Charge. If space is tight, don’t insist on keeping two axes active; keep just one. Save Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt enemies diving onto your allied damage dealers. Avoid grouping in one spot to prepare for Ziggs's R Mega Inferno Bomb.
Ziggs.build: The information provided isn’t enough to determine a specific first item to buy. Build magic resistance rather than armor to defend against Ziggs’s main damage. Movement speed also helps you get out of the impact areas of Ziggs Q Bouncing Bomb and Ziggs R Mega Inferno Bomb.
Ziggs.escape: Right after Ziggs W Satchel Charge has been used is your chance to close the gap. If Ziggs E Hexplosive Minefield has been laid down, don't engage through it; first find an approach from a direction without mines.
Ziggs.phase: Draven is strongest in lane, so build an early lead with kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, turn that gold into turrets and objectives, but don’t leave a wave unattended in front of an allied turret when its health is low. In the late game, there are fewer safe places to catch axes, so cut back on risky chases.
Ziggs.watch: Stepping on Ziggs E Hexplosive Minefield slows you and makes it harder to dodge his follow-up abilities, so take a route without mines or wait for them to disappear. When the warning area for Ziggs R Mega Inferno Bomb appears, move away from the blast center even if you can’t get completely out of range.

Nilah.watch: When Nilah W Jubilant Veil is active, your basic attacks miss, so stop basic attacks and keep your distance until it ends. Right after Nilah Q Formless Blade hits, Nilah gains attack range and her attacks deal area damage, so step back farther. When Nilah E Slipstream dashes in, interrupt the dash with Draven E Stand Aside. If Nilah has R Apotheosis available, keep your distance from allies.
Nilah.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Nilah Q Formless Blade, Nilah E Slipstream, and Nilah R Apotheosis. Also build health because Nilah Q Formless Blade has penetration. If healing continues for a prolonged period during fights, or the enemy support also provides healing, buy Executioner's Calling earlier.
Nilah.fight: When Nilah goes for a last hit, briefly trade with an empowered Draven Q Spinning Axe basic attack from outside her range. Stop basic attacks while Nilah W Jubilant Veil is active, then attack again after it ends. If Nilah E Slipstream closes the gap, interrupt it with your saved Draven E Stand Aside and create distance again.
Nilah.laning: Give up the axe if the spot where Draven Q Spinning Axe will land is toward Nilah or a brush. Before stepping forward to catch an axe, check the minimap and maintain vision in the brush and river.
Nilah.combo: Just before engaging, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe, land an empowered basic attack, then move to the axe's landing spot. Use Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe to reset its cooldown as you catch it, then follow up with the next empowered basic attack. If Nilah E Slipstream engages, interrupt it with Draven E Stand Aside. Stop your basic attack sequence when Nilah W Jubilant Veil is active.
Nilah.escape: Nilah E Slipstream has a short cooldown, so don't push in deep just because she used it. Your chance to attack comes after Nilah engages and has fully expended Nilah W Jubilant Veil as well. If she tries to close the gap again with Nilah E Slipstream, interrupt it with Draven E Stand Aside.
Nilah.phase: Draven is strong in the early laning phase, so pressure Nilah when she goes for melee last hits to gain CS and Turret Plating. In the mid game, quickly convert that gold into towers and objectives. In the late game, there is less room to catch axes safely, so avoid forcing an engage.
Nilah.teamfight: Let your allies start the fight, then attack from a safe position after Nilah's engage ability is down. Spread out so several allies aren't caught by Nilah R Apotheosis, and interrupt Nilah E Slipstream when she dashes onto an allied damage dealer with Draven E Stand Aside. If space is tight, don't risk trying to keep two Draven Q Spinning Axe axes active; safely maintain just one.

Yasuo.watch: Yasuo can use minions to close in with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade, so don't step forward to catch an axe where there are many minions. After Yasuo Q Steel Tempest hits twice, watch for the knock-up tornado and dodge sideways instead of retreating in a straight line. When Yasuo W Wind Wall appears, go around it or save your key abilities until it disappears.
Yasuo.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest and Yasuo R Last Breath. Armor cannot block the magic damage from Yasuo E Sweeping Blade. If attack speed reduction is also an option, it slows both Yasuo's basic attack frequency and how often his tornado becomes available.
Yasuo.fight: Trigger Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer's shield with a basic attack before committing to a full trade. Your chance to attack comes right after Yasuo launches his tornado and his stacks reset. If Yasuo E Sweeping Blade closes in, interrupt the dash with Draven E Stand Aside and regain your distance.
Yasuo.combo: Before a fight, activate Draven Q Spinning Axe and use a basic attack to trigger Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer's shield first. Activate Draven W Blood Rush just before catching the axe, then catch it and land the next empowered basic attack. If Yasuo E Sweeping Blade engages, interrupt it with your saved Draven E Stand Aside.
Yasuo.escape: Right after Yasuo launches his tornado, he won't have a knock-up available for a while, so look for an opening to engage. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade comes back quickly, so don't push in deep just because he used it once. Before Yasuo R Last Breath is available again, look for an opening to interrupt his movement with Draven E Stand Aside when crowd control can be chained together.
Yasuo.phase: Draven is strong with axes in the early laning phase, so use safe basic attack pressure to aim for kills, CS, and Turret Plating. In the mid game, quickly convert the gold you've earned into towers and objectives. In the late game, there is less room to catch axes safely, so avoid forcing solo fights.
Yasuo.teamfight: Let your allies engage first, then use basic attacks from a safe position after Yasuo's engage ability is down. If space is tight, don't risk trying to keep two axes active; maintain just one. Save Draven E Stand Aside to interrupt Yasuo when he engages onto an allied damage dealer.
Yasuo.laning: Keep the wave small and pushed toward your side to reduce the minions Yasuo E Sweeping Blade can use as stepping stones. If Draven Q Spinning Axe will land toward Yasuo, give up the axe and apply pressure from a safe distance. Before moving out to catch an axe, check the minimap and maintain vision in the brush and river in that direction.
